    Optimal Sample Size Calculation for a Paired Comparative Diagnostic Accuracy Study with Co-Primary Endpoints

    paired_ss_opt_bin.Rd

    The function determines the minimal total sample size per group that guarantees the desired overall power for a paired comparative diagnostic accuracy study with co-primary endpoints (sensitivity and specificity) using the intersection–union testing framework (IUT).

    In a paired design, each subject receives the experimental test, the comparator test and the reference standard.

    The study is evaluated under the intersection–union testing (IUT) framework: both endpoint-specific null hypotheses must be rejected for overall study success. Under this framework, the global Type I error rate is controlled at level \(\alpha\) without multiplicity adjustment.

    Superiority and non-inferiority hypotheses may be specified independently for sensitivity and specificity.

    paired_ss_opt_bin(
  power,
  prev,
  se.c,
  se.e,
  sp.c,
  sp.e,
  psi.d,
  psi.nd,
  alpha,
  delta.se = 0,
  delta.sp = 0,
  type.se = c("sup", "ni"),
  type.sp = c("sup", "ni")
)

    Arguments

    power

    Overall desired power for the co-primary hypothesis.

    prev

    Disease prevalence in the study population.

    se.c

    Sensitivity of the comparator test.

    se.e

    Sensitivity of the experimental test.

    sp.c

    Specificity of the comparator test.

    sp.e

    Specificity of the experimental test.

    psi.d

    discordant test results for diseased patients

    psi.nd

    discordant test results for non-diseased patients

    alpha

    Type I error rate per endpoint.

    delta.se

    Non-inferiority margin for sensitivity (used only if type.se = "ni").

    delta.sp

    Non-inferiority margin for specificity (used only if type.sp = "ni").

    type.se

    Type of hypothesis for sensitivity: "sup" (superiority, default) or "ni" (non-inferiority).

    type.sp

    Type of hypothesis for specificity: "sup" (superiority, default) or "ni" (non-inferiority).

    Value

    An object of class "dx_bin" containing:

    • design specifications(design specifications (alpha level, testing framework)

    • required total sample size per group,

    • subgroup sample sizes (diseased / non-diseased),

    • target overall power

    • allocated endpoint-specific powers.

    Details

    Design framework

    Sensitivity is evaluated in the diseased subgroup and specificity in the non-diseased subgroup.

    With total sample size \(N\) and disease prevalence \(\pi\), subgroup sizes are:

    $$N_{Se} = N\pi, \qquad N_{Sp} = N(1-\pi).$$

    Intersection–Union Testing (IUT)

    The global null hypothesis is the union of the endpoint-specific null hypotheses. Study success requires rejection of both endpoint-specific hypotheses.

    Assuming independence between diseased and non-diseased subgroups, the overall power is:

    $$Power_{overall} = Power_{Se} \times Power_{Sp}.$$

    Hypothesis specification

    Let \(\theta_{Se,E}\) and \(\theta_{Se,C}\) denote the sensitivities of the experimental and comparator tests, and \(\theta_{Sp,E}\) and \(\theta_{Sp,C}\) the corresponding specificities.

    Superiority (both endpoints):

    $$ H_{0,global} = (\theta_{Se,E} \le \theta_{Se,C}) \cup (\theta_{Sp,E} \le \theta_{Sp,C}) $$

    Sensitivity superiority and specificity non-inferiority:

    Let \(\Delta_{Sp} > 0\) denote the NI margin for specificity.

    $$ H_{0,global} = (\theta_{Se,E} \le \theta_{Se,C}) \cup (\theta_{Sp,E} \le \theta_{Sp,C} - \Delta_{Sp}) $$

    Similar formulations apply for other combinations of superiority and non-inferiority.

    Endpoint-specific sample size formulas

    Let \(d = \theta_E - \theta_C\) denote the difference between the experimental and comparator test (sensitivity or specificity, depending on the endpoint).

    For each endpoint, the required subgroup sample size is derived from the large-sample normal approximation of the corresponding paired test statistic.

    For superiority hypotheses (\(H_0: d \le 0\)), the sample size is obtained from the asymptotic power formula for paired binary data described by Miettinen (1968) and applied in Stark et al. (2022). The required number of subjects is determined by solving the power equation with respect to the sample size.

    For non-inferiority hypotheses (\(H_0: d \le -\Delta\)), the sample size is derived from the score test for paired binary data described by Liu et al. (2002). The asymptotic power function of the score statistic, with variance evaluated at the non-inferiority boundary (\(d = -\Delta\)) using a restricted maximum likelihood (RMLE) approach, is solved numerically to obtain the required sample size.

    To achieve a desired overall power, the function determines endpoint-specific type II error rates \(\beta_{Se}\) and \(\beta_{Sp}\) satisfying:

    $$(1-\beta_{Se})(1-\beta_{Sp}) = power.$$

    The total sample size is chosen such that the required subgroup sizes are simultaneously satisfied.

    Required assumptions (nuisance parameters)

    In addition to sensitivities and specificities, the paired design requires assumptions on:

    • Disease prevalence: \(\pi\)

    • Discordant proportion among diseased subjects: \(\psi_D\)

    • Discordant proportion among non-diseased subjects: \(\psi_{ND}\)

    These are nuisance parameters and must be specified based on prior studies or clinical knowledge. Discordant parameters must satisfy the theoretical bounds.

    For diseased subjects:

    $$ |Se_C - Se_E| \le \psi_D \le Se_C + Se_E - 2 Se_C Se_E $$

    For non-diseased subjects:

    $$ |Sp_C - Sp_E| \le \psi_{ND} \le Sp_C + Sp_E - 2 Sp_C Sp_E $$

    Minimal discordance values are therefore:

    $$\psi_{D,min} = |Se_C - Se_E|$$ $$\psi_{ND,min} = |Sp_C - Sp_E|$$

    In practice, the sample size may be calculated using these minimal values together with an assumed (true) prevalence \(\pi_{ass}.\)

    Important assumptions

    • Asymptotic normal approximation is used.

    • Diseased and non-diseased subgroups are treated as independent.

    • The true effect must satisfy the alternative hypothesis (e.g., \(d + \Delta > 0\) for non-inferiority).

    References

    Stark, M., Hesse, M., Brannath, W., & Zapf, A. (2022). Blinded sample size re-estimation in a comparative diagnostic accuracy study. BMC Medical Research Methodology, 22, 115. doi:10.1186/s12874-022-01564-2

    Liu, J. P., Hsueh, H. M., Hsieh, E., & Chen, J. J. (2002). Tests for equivalence or non-inferiority for paired binary data. Statistics in Medicine, 21(2), 231–245. doi:10.1002/sim.1012

    Miettinen, O.S. (1968). The matched pairs design in the case of all-or-none responses. Biometrics, 24(2), 339–352. doi:10.2307/2528039

    See also

    paired_power_opt_bin for power determination, ss_opt_bin and power_opt_bin for single-test design unpaired_ss_opt_bin and unpaired_power_opt_bin for unpaired designs.

    Maia Muresan (DCR Bern)

    Examples

    
# Example 1: Superiority for both sensitivity and specificity
# The experimental test is assumed superior on both endpoints
paired_ss_opt_bin(
  alpha = 0.05,
  power = 0.80,          # desired overall power
  se.c = 0.81,           # comparator sensitivity
  se.e = 0.90,           # experimental sensitivity
  sp.c = 0.66,           # comparator specificity
  sp.e = 0.80,           # experimental specificity
  psi.d = 0.09,          # discordance (diseased subgroup)
  psi.nd = 0.14,         # discordance (non-diseased subgroup)
  prev = 0.5             # disease prevalence
)
#> 
#> DxPower - Confirmatory Diagnostic Accuracy Study 
#> --------------------------------------------------
#> Design:            paired comparative design 
#> Framework:        Co-primary (IUT)
#> Alpha level:       0.05 
#> Prevalence:        0.5 
#> 
#> Hypotheses:
#>   Sensitivity :    sup 
#>   Specificity :    sup 
#> 
#> Required sample size per group:
#>   Total:           127 
#>   Diseased:        64 
#>   Non-diseased:    64 
#> 
#> Target overall power:   0.8 
#> 
#> Allocated powers:
#>   Sensitivity:      0.812 
#>   Specificity:      0.985 
#> 


# Explicit superiority specification (same as default)
paired_ss_opt_bin(
  alpha = 0.05,
  power = 0.80,
  se.c = 0.81, se.e = 0.90,
  sp.c = 0.66, sp.e = 0.80,
  psi.d = 0.09,
  psi.nd = 0.14,
  prev = 0.5,
  type.se = "sup",
  type.sp = "sup"
)
#> 
#> DxPower - Confirmatory Diagnostic Accuracy Study 
#> --------------------------------------------------
#> Design:            paired comparative design 
#> Framework:        Co-primary (IUT)
#> Alpha level:       0.05 
#> Prevalence:        0.5 
#> 
#> Hypotheses:
#>   Sensitivity :    sup 
#>   Specificity :    sup 
#> 
#> Required sample size per group:
#>   Total:           127 
#>   Diseased:        64 
#>   Non-diseased:    64 
#> 
#> Target overall power:   0.8 
#> 
#> Allocated powers:
#>   Sensitivity:      0.812 
#>   Specificity:      0.985 
#> 

# Example 2: Sensitivity superiority and specificity non-inferiority
# Non-inferiority margin for specificity = 0.10
# Note: Experimental test is superior to the comparator test regarding sensitivity
# and non-inferior regarding specificity .
paired_ss_opt_bin(
  alpha = 0.05,
  power = 0.80,
  se.c = 0.81, se.e = 0.90,
  sp.c = 0.66, sp.e = 0.80,
  psi.d = 0.09,
  psi.nd = 0.14,
  prev = 0.5,
  delta.sp = 0.10,       # non-inferiority margin for specificity
  type.sp = "ni"
)
#> 
#> DxPower - Confirmatory Diagnostic Accuracy Study 
#> --------------------------------------------------

#> Prevalence:        0.5
